gaps.note: Monad. theme-monad-native-path shows that every public node serving call traces runs block execution with the interpreter only (main.cpp 484-488 at v0.16.7). So every mined Monad swap, removal and replay in cycles 10 to 14, including the 129,567 mined 512 bit mulDiv instances found this cycle, is interpreter output of an RPC node. None of it is compiled-code output. The step that would tie that output to validators that may run compiled code is the delayed merkle root. The Monad docs say proposals carry the state root of block N-D, that delayed root validity is part of block validity, and that a node whose execution differs falls out of consensus and re-executes (https://docs.monad.xyz/monad-arch/consensus/asynchronous-execution, found by critic search on 2026-11-24). No unit has read that check in the v0.16.7 source or tested it. Critic query on 2026-11-24: rpc.monad.xyz reports Monad/0.16.7 and block 125,134,719 has stateRoot 0xb49ece27...65e4. Nobody has asked whether that field is the node's own root or the consensus delayed root.

HyperEVM. theme-producer-operands found producer evidence for the 512 bit MULMOD and mulDiv operand classes on MegaETH from 3,741 mined v3 style swaps (L-701). It did not do the same on HyperEVM, whose validator is closed and has only about 2,800 PoolManager transactions in its whole history. The hyperevm unit reran the RPC battery and nothing else. For the closed producer, the branches with no mined instance (the overflow fallback of SqrtPriceMath, amounts above 2^160, the Q128 copy of mulDiv at pc 22358, swaps ending on an initialized tick) still rest on the archive client and the official RPC node, which may not be the code that writes blocks.

Celo. Critic queries of forno.celo.org on 2026-11-24 returned reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb three times and Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817/linux-amd64/go1.24.13 once. The verifier of theme-reth-cache-drift saw the same thing. Cycle 9 tested two Celo backends, but this go1.24.13 op-geth build is dated 17 August 2026 and no cycle has tied it to a source commit. No Celo unit ran in cycle 14. A load balanced endpoint mixes the answers of two clients, so a vector that passed does not say which client passed it.

Upcoming forks. Only ethereum-reference carried the forks angle this cycle, and it covered Glamsterdam only. OPCODES.md names Tempo T14 and BNB Chain Jenner on 8 December 2026 inside the deployment window, Tempo T15 (zone deposit forwarding from inside the token precompile), Monad v0.16.6 and later (new compiled shift path) and bor v2.12 (MULMOD memo, precompile cache). No unit this cycle read the next scheduled upgrade for the OP Stack chains after Karst, for Arc, for Avalanche or for Polygon.

Arc. On 2026-11-24 rpc.mainnet.arc.io answered web3_clientVersion with arc/v1 and arc_getVersion with v0.8.6-rc1 (37812c61), the same as cycle 13 (critic queries). The other two public endpoints (v0.8.5 and v0.8.6) and the release the permissioned validators run are still untested. No Arc unit ran in cycle 14.

MegaETH. The stateless validator (L-626) was not run for the fifth cycle. The reth execution cache question for mega-reth v2.2.3-72527bc (critic query: mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc answers mega-reth/v2.2.3-72527bc) was left unknown by theme-reth-cache-drift. Producer evidence exists for the 512 bit product only. Nothing covers the clear, allowance or operator paths or swaps that end on an initialized tick, because MegaETH has 0 Donate, 0 Approval and 0 OperatorSet logs in its whole history.

leads.question: In Monad v0.16.7, does a non-validating full node, and in particular one started with --trace-calls, compare the root it computes for block N-D with the delayed merkle root that consensus carries in block N, and does it stop or re-execute on a mismatch? Name the file and line. Is the stateRoot in eth_getBlockByNumber the node's own root or the consensus root? Check this for a few recent blocks against the delayed root field in a later block's header.
leads.why: If the tracing nodes check their roots against the consensus roots, then every mined Monad result of cycles 10 to 14 (more than 600,000 swaps and the 129,567 instances of the 512 bit branch) becomes evidence about the state validators commit, whatever execution mode they run. If they do not check, compiled code on validators is still untested. A miscompile in FullMath or SqrtPriceMath on that path could be used by any account that sends a swap with the right operands.

leads.question: Find the highest-volume Uniswap v3 style pools on HyperEVM (read their factories' PoolCreated logs from the archive client). For every mined swap in the last 2,000,000 blocks whose relation needs a product above 2^256, or an amount above 2^160, or a price on an initialized tick boundary, does the logged result match the exact FullMath and SqrtPriceMath formula to the unit? Use the method theme-producer-operands applied to MegaETH for L-701.
leads.why: This is the only way to get producer evidence from the closed HyperEVM validator for the operand classes that no PoolManager transaction there has reached. A difference would be a validator-only arithmetic result that any account could reach through a swap.

leads.question: Build the v0.16.7 x86 emitter with stubbed runtime symbols and print estimate_size() for the 24,009 byte PoolManager runtime. Is it below the 778,528 byte bound, so that hot validators compile the PoolManager at all?
leads.why: If the estimate is above the bound, Monad's compiled path never runs the PoolManager and the open Monad items reduce to the interpreter, which is already tested. If it is below, the delayed root lead above becomes the only evidence for the compiled path. This merges L-648, L-672 and L-676.

leads.question: Pin the forno.celo.org request to the Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817 backend: repeat each request until web3_clientVersion is the same before and after. Do battery.py, targeted.py, callsem.py and pmdiff.py give the recorded results on that backend? Which repository and commit is c7ed55b8?
leads.why: One of the two clients behind the official Celo endpoint is unidentified, and the reruns mix it with reth. If that backend also follows the chain for any production role, a result from it that differs would matter. This continues the theme-reth-cache-drift verifier lead and F-116.

leads.question: Does mega-reth v2.2.3-72527bc carry the reth execution cache branch that keeps cached storage words of a re-created account without code? Does MegaETH's sequencer read state through that cache? Answer from public mega-reth source or from the mega-evm lock and reth revision it names.
leads.why: On the network whose producer is closed, a stale storage read there would be committed state, and no second client would catch it. This is the open link of the theme-reth-cache-drift transfer.

leads.question: Which path in an ordinary block puts a storage word for an address without code into the reth execution cache before the block that destroys and re-creates that address? Candidates are the prewarm of an EIP-2930 access list, a block access list prefetch, or an SLOAD against a codeless address from a contract. Can such a word reach any read made by the PoolManager, a token's balanceOf, or a hook in a pool without attacker code?
leads.why: This settles both theme-reth-cache-drift findings, which are plausible on this one link. If the word exists but never reaches a PoolManager read, both findings stay at follower-stall level.

leads.question: Does the Tempo v1.19.1 node binary depend on reth crates with default features, now that reth v2.11 makes the evm2 LLVM compiler a default feature? Is the JitBackend that ethereum-reference found built even with jit disabled present in Tempo's EVM config? Read bin/ and crates/node Cargo.toml at tempo/v1.19.1 and the release workflow's cargo flags.
leads.why: Transfer from the ethereum-reference finding. On Ethereum a JIT fault reaches one node of a diverse client set. Tempo has no second client, so a JIT that its validators turned on would decide canonical state for FullMath and TickMath. OPCODES.md says the published binaries are built without JIT, but that was read before reth changed its defaults.

leads.question: At evm2 66687c18 (Ethereum reth v2.11.0) and 35aa3280 (Tempo v1.19.1), does the JIT emit MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 and with the constant moduli 2^96 and 2^128, SDIV and SMOD at -2^255 / -1, SAR by 255, and SIGNEXTEND from bytes 2 and 15 as the specification requires? Transcribe the LLVM IR builders for those opcodes and run them on the targeted vectors.
leads.why: This is the ethereum-reference lead extended to Tempo. It is the arithmetic a JIT-enabled node runs for every swap, and no eth_call can reach it.

leads.question: After 8 December 2026 (BNB Chain Jenner at 02:30 UTC, Tempo T14 at Unix time 1796742000), rerun battery.py, targeted.py, callsem.py, statekeys.py and pmdiff6.py on both networks. Does any instruction table, transient storage or call-gas rule change for the PoolManager?

leads.question: For each network other than Ethereum, Tempo and BNB Smart Chain, name the next scheduled or proposed execution upgrade with a date before May 2027 from the network's official upgrade page. Does it change an opcode, add a precompile or system contract at an address the PoolManager can be made to call (P1, P2, P3), or change transaction-boundary semantics for transient storage?
leads.why: The upcoming-forks angle ran only for Ethereum this cycle. A precompile that is added at a known address and answers transfer or balanceOf with the PoolManager as msg.sender is the kind of change that would make P2 or P3 move pooled funds.

leads.question: Under Tempo's T15 code in v1.19.1, which addresses are zone deposit addresses? Can an ordinary account create one or name one as `to` in take(token, to, amount), so that a TIP-20 transfer from the PoolManager is forwarded to a portal by a call from inside the token precompile? Does that forwarded call run with the PoolManager as the depositor, and can its outcome differ from the amount the token debits?
leads.why: If T15 activates while the PoolManager holds TIP-20 balances, a forwarding that the chain does inside a transfer is a chain-level change to P2. It is the one transfer-path change found in the client code that no unit has read.

leads.question: Can HyperCore emit an unsigned system transfer from a contract address that no spot token links and no storage slot names, as it did for 0xc20699185c15D0a2fD65779BB5d69f5b0B113c00? Answer from the node's published system transaction rules or by finding the HyperCore action that produced the first such transfer for that address.
leads.why: This is the one remaining link of F-020. The verifier's storage reading shows that the PoolManager cannot be linked through finalizeEvmContract today.

leads.question: Does the consensus-v61 replay WebAssembly module, compiled by Nitro's JIT validator with wasmer Cranelift 0.129.1, contain a function with more than 2^24 SSA values or a br_table near the aarch64 reach limit of the October 2026 advisories? Count both from the module enforced by wasmModuleRoot 0xc10cd7ec...dc97.
leads.why: The arbitrum-family unit closed the Cranelift advisories for Stylus only. The replay binary is also JIT compiled on validators. A wrong result there changes validators' assertions, although the on-chain one-step proof would still decide a dispute.

leads.question: bor v2.12.0-beta adds --precompile-cache, which is off by default. What key does it use, and is it the full input bytes and the precompile address? Could a cached result be returned for a STATICCALL that the PoolManager makes in sync(X) when X is a precompile?
